The Wall Street Journal reported that Apple has been actively negotiating content deals worth nine figures to enhance Siri AI's ability to access the latest news. Details below.

Apple in talks with publishers for content to power Siri AI

According to a report published today by The Wall Street Journal, Apple has been engaging with multiple publishers, hoping to reach multi-year partnership agreements to give Siri AI access to current events and informational content.

The report points out:

Apple's move comes as publishers are increasingly caught between "taking AI companies to court" and "licensing content to them." For example, The New York Times is suing OpenAI and Microsoft over the alleged unauthorised use of its content to train AI models; at the same time, publishers such as News Corp and Axel Springer have chosen to enter content licensing agreements with the developer of ChatGPT.

Reddit is similarly pursuing a dual-track approach — on one hand, it reached an agreement with Google in 2024 to license content for AI training (currently under review), reportedly worth around US$60 million per year; on the other hand, it has filed lawsuits against Anthropic and Perplexity respectively over alleged unauthorised scraping of its data.

Returning to The Wall Street Journal's report, it mentions that this type of deal is not new for Apple, as the company is already partnering with publishers to operate Apple News+, and has previously reached agreements including licensing publishers' content for its own AI training purposes.

The Wall Street Journal has reached out to Apple for comment on the matter, but the latter declined to comment.
